title: Sort names with a comparator lambda instead of an anonymous class

blocks.text: Before Java 8, sorting with a custom order meant writing an anonymous inner class that implements `Comparator<String>`. A lambda, or a method reference such as `String::compareTo`, passes the same behaviour in one line.
Write two methods in `NameSorter`, each taking a `List<String>` and returning a **new** sorted list:

items: `byLength(List<String> names)` orders them by length, shortest first; names of the same length are ordered alphabetically.

blocks.text: Think about what happens to the list the caller handed you, and about names that tie on length.

cases.says: It returns the names in alphabetical order.
It returns the names shortest first.
The caller's list keeps its order; the sorted names come back in a new list.
Names of equal length are ordered alphabetically, not left in input order.

concepts: A lambda passes behaviour as an argument, replacing a verbose anonymous inner class such as a Comparator.
